sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cloud Vulnerability Scanning and Penetration Testing SaaS

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between France and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion (1994, as amended by the 2006 and 2009 Protocols)
OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (amended 2010, in force for France)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between the EU and Canada (provisionally applied since 21 September 2017)
France-China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1984, as amended by the Protocol of 2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-49 and R.561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT duties, UBO identification); Loi n° 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II) on transparency and corruption prevention; Ordonnance n° 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849; Décret n° 2018-284 of 18 April 2018 establishing the French beneficial-ownership register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE); Article L.123-33 of the Code de commerce (RBE filing with the RNE); Article L.561-2-1 CMF (25% UBO threshold); Article L.561-46 CMF (register filing). Following ECJ joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 (22 November 2022), access to the RBE is restricted to government authorities and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the natural-person shareholder/UBO identity document (passport) and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public authority of the shareholder's country (mayor, consulate or notary) for the certified copy; apostille issued by the designated apostille authority of that country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or French consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / corporate KYC extract of the corporate shareholder from its domestic commercial registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or chamber of commerce in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or French consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation of the corporate and identity documents filed with the RNE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn court translator (traducteur assermenté) registered with a French Cour d'appel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for the underlying foreign documents; the translation itself requires no apostille and is certified by the translator's seal)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly legalized power of attorney (pouvoir) for the representative signing the incorporation filing and domiciliation agreement on behalf of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or other competent legal authority in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or French consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory at incorporation: screening of shareholders, directors, and UBOs against the EU consolidated financial-sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list (for USD-denominated Stripe and wire-transfer rails), and French asset-freezing orders (arrêtés de gel des avoirs). PEP categorization per Articles L.561-10 and R.561-10 CMF (senior public officials as defined by Directive (EU) 2015/849). Screening results must be archived in the KYC file. TRACFIN suspicious-transaction reporting (Article L.561-15 CMF) applies to the banking and payment providers for this low-risk, non-regulated SaaS. Dual-use and intrusion-software export controls (EU Regulation 2021/821, Annex I items 4A005 and cyber-surveillance items) must additionally be screened because penetration-testing services may be subject to prior authorization or notification to the French Ministry of Economy.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet des Entreprises (www.guichet-entreprises.gouv.fr) - official single filing portal; Registre national des entreprises (RNE) administered by the INPI (data.inpi.fr) for availability and trademark conflict searches
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The articles of association, RNE declaration and all exhibits must be drafted in French. The corporate name may contain foreign-language terms, but the RNE/RCS records are maintained in Latin script, requiring a Latin-script transliteration for non-Latin names. The name must be distinctive and must not mislead as to legal form, public affiliation, nationality, or regulated activity; the suffix 'SAS' must be indicated in all corporate communications.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not provide a distinct statutory name-reservation period within the RCS process; the 30-day figure represents the practical planning window for re-verification of availability on the RNE and INPI databases immediately before filing. On rejection of the proposed name by the Guichet/INPI registry on grounds of confusing similarity or prohibited token, the applicant may: (1) refile with a corrected name through the Guichet des Entreprises without an additional state fee for the correction; (2) apply to the competent ministerial or sector-regulator authority (e.g., ACPR for 'Banque', competent ministry for 'France') for prior authorization of the sensitive token; (3) appeal the registry refusal before the President of the Tribunal judiciaire within two months of notification, based on Articles L.123-33 and R.123-54 of the Code de commerce; and (4) if the objection is grounded on a prior trademark, contest the opposition under Articles L.711-3 and L.716-4-10 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Lawful for a low-risk cybersecurity SaaS. The SAS must have a real French registered address (siège social), but a licensed business-domiciliation provider (société de domiciliation, Article L.123-11-2 of the Code de commerce) may serve as the registered office. The arrangement must include a physical French address, permanent staff reception of mail and registered letters, and a written domiciliation agreement; a mere post-office box is insufficient. For this non-regulated infosec SaaS, no additional ministerial authorization for domiciliation is required.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SAS articles of association (statuts) and corporate governance package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard SAS with one or more foreign shareholders (typically EUR 2,500-4,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication of the incorporation notice in an approved legal announcements journal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) approved by the prefecture
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory press tariff (typically EUR 75-200 per insertion)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official RNE/company-creation filing fee via the Guichet des Entreprises (including frais de greffe)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI and Greffe du Tribunal de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory State fee schedule (approximately EUR 60-110 for SAS incorporation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation service (annual fee, virtual office option)
Apostille/consular legalization and sworn French translation of shareholder and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille/consular authority of the documents' country of origin; sworn translator (traducteur assermenté)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular/apostille fee schedules plus per-page translator tariffs (EUR 50-90 per page)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT due diligence: PEP and sanctions screening of UBOs and preparation of the beneficial-ownership declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk non-financial SaaS

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account/KYC onboarding support for wire-transfer and Stripe settlement rails
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank or external fintech onboarding agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for non-regulated business accounts; bank account fees invoiced separately

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Book II, Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-20 for SAS; general corporate provisions Articles L. 210-1 et seq.; Décret n° 67-236 relating to company registers; French Civil Code Articles 1832 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; national electronic interface via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; INSEE for SIREN/SIRET issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de la Société (Articles of Association) submitted with the single incorporation application (Formulaire M0) to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SAS; capital is freely set in the articles. Cash contributions must be deposited with a bank or notary before incorporation, and at least one-half of cash contributions must be paid up upon incorporation (balance within five years). In-kind contributions must be fully delivered at subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the founders accept the subscriptions to the share capital of the SAS as stated in the attendance sheet and the articles, and certify that the capital is fully subscribed and legally paid; RESOLVED that the final Statuts are adopted and that the registered office be fixed at the address shown in the articles; RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed President and [Name] as General Manager, each with the powers conferred by law and the Statuts; RESOLVED that the President is authorized to carry out all incorporation formalities, including legal publication and RCS filing; RESOLVED that all prior acts performed in the corporate interest are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name verification and preparation of articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) / Infogreffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the INPI trademark database and the Infogreffe RCS database for identical or confusing prior names. Optionally reserve the chosen company name. Draft and finalize the Statuts in French or bilingual form. Have each shareholder sign every page of the articles and initial the annexes. If a corporate shareholder or director is involved, appoint a natural-person representative.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for any representative signatory
Identity documents of shareholders and director(s)
Declaration of non-conviction and non-concurrent mandates (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search flags a conflict or trademark risk, the founding parties may modify the company name and revise the Statuts accordingly, or submit evidence of coexistence/licence from the prior rights holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and publication of legal notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank or notary; Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) of the registered office department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account or notarial escrow for cash contributions and deposit the share capital. Obtain the capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds). Prepare and publish the legal notice of incorporation (avis de constitution) in an authorized legal gazette within the department where the registered office is located.
required_dossiers: Bank or notary capital deposit certificate
Legal notice text for the JAL
Certified articles (to be sent with the notice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit certificate is challenged or incomplete, obtain a corrected attestation from the bank/notary and, if necessary, re-run the legal notice publication after correcting the filing text.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of incorporation application to the Greffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce du lieu du siège social via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the unified incorporation application (Formulaire M0) electronically. Attach the signed Statuts, capital deposit certificate, proof of legal publication (attestation de parution), identity documents of directors, and declarations of non-conviction. The first president or authorized representative signs the application electronically.
required_dossiers: Attestation de dépôt des fonds (capital deposit certificate)
Identity documents of shareholders and directors
Declaration of non-conviction and non-concurrent mandates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe queries the dossier, the applicant must respond through the online platform within the stated deadline, correct or supplement any missing or defective attachments, and resubmit the amended application without additional company action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of K-bis
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) via the Greffe; Registre National des Entreprises (RNE/INSEE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Greffe approves the application, the company is assigned an RCS number and a SIREN/SIRET. Verify the data displayed on the RNE public portal. If necessary, file a modification declaration (form M&O) within 10 days for any inconsistency in management appointments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis or SIRET data contains an error, file a request for rectification using the M&O modification form through the same online channel or by directly addressing the Greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF, DREETS (conseil départemental), and the official business portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer for payroll social security. Complete the workplace registration and, if applicable, the CSE (employee representative) setup when the payroll reaches 11 employees. For pure cloud SaaS activities, no environmental classified installation (ICPE) filing is required. Update the company website legal notice and, if applicable, appoint a Data Protection Officer for full GDPR alignment.
required_dossiers: Employee declarations or work contract list (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a declaration is missing or rejected, use the single portal at entreprendre.service-public.fr to resubmit the specific form with the required attachments, keeping the original filing receipts for compliance evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — pure digital and SaaS service; no industrial plant or ICPE-classified installation (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement). For product-related security certification, consult ANSSI (Agence Nationale de la Sécurité des Systèmes d'Information) on a voluntary basis.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for cloud vulnerability scanning and penetration testing SaaS under ISIC 6201; no manufacturing or operating permit is applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique / DREETS (regional environmental enforcement) — no substantive application due to service nature
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical discharge, industrial effluent, or volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions arising from the SaaS activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the company's core operations. Indirect energy consumption is attributable to the cloud provider's data centers, which must comply with EU sustainability reporting and energy efficiency requirements. Office premises must follow standard waste segregation (déchets d'activités économiques) and building energy regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office-only operations do not require a special pre-occupancy fire certificate for private premises; however, the employer must maintain evacuation procedures, accessible fire extinguishers, and conduct a workplace risk assessment. For buildings open to the public, the préfecture may impose a safety commission review. Employer obligations include displaying emergency instructions and, from 11 employees, establishing a CSE (Comité Social et Économique).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; business portal: pro.impots.gouv.fr; general portal: impots.gouv.fr; customs portal: douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entity establishing a French SAS: (1) file incorporation through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); (2) DGFIP automatically attributes SIREN and SIRET; (3) VAT registration occurs together with company registration, resulting in an intra-Community TVA number in the Sirene registry. For a foreign seller with no French fixed establishment, use the Union OSS/Non-Union OSS or IOSS portals for eligible distance sales and digital services; for pure B2B operations, apply for simplified French VAT registration at the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) and obtain a France-specific TVA number. Non-EU sellers without a fixed establishment must ordinarily appoint a DGFIP-accredited fiscal representative under Article 289 A of the French General Tax Code (CGI) before registering for VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not maintain a US-style check-the-box election. The default for an SAS is mandatory corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Specific elections include: (i) option for income-tax treatment under Article 239 bis AB CGI for qualifying small/young companies; (ii) election to form a French tax consolidation group (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI where at least 95% of capital is held; (iii) hybrid-mismatch outcomes are not elective and follow the EU ATAD transposition rules under Article 212-0 et seq. CGI, requiring documentation of any mismatch treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established company, no turnover threshold exists; VAT registration is mandatory before carrying on any taxable activity. For an EU seller making intra-EU distance sales of goods to French consumers, the applicable cross-border distance-sales registration threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year (option to register below this threshold exists). For a non-EU seller supplying digital or B2C services into France, there is no monetary threshold; registration is required through the Non-Union OSS scheme or direct French VAT registration. For B2B supplies, a non-established foreign seller of services to a French taxable customer is not required to register in France because the place of supply is at the customer's location and reverse-charge applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is not a real-time fiscal stamping jurisdiction. Under the French e-invoicing reform (2022 administrative simplification law), B2B e-invoicing is mandatory for established taxable persons through a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) connected to the public Portal Public de Facturation (PPF); B2C and international transaction data are subject to mandatory e-reporting. The rollout is phased: large and mid-sized entities must issue e-invoices from 1 September 2026 and small businesses from 1 September 2027. Standardised formats include Factur-X, UBL, CII, Peppol BIS; API connectivity is required. No DGFIP clearance stamp is applied to individual invoices; transmission is periodic, accompanied by audit-trail retention requirements. OSS/IOSS filings use separate European Commission portal infrastructure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods qualify for the 0% export rate (exemption with right to input VAT deduction) when the goods are physically delivered to a destination outside the EU; proof of dispatch and EU exit is mandatory. Offshore services and cross-border digital services supplied to a non-resident business customer are treated as made outside France under the B2B place-of-supply rule in Article 259-A CGI; therefore they are outside French territoriality rather than formally zero-rated. For a cybersecurity SaaS product supplied to a non-EU enterprise, no French VAT should be applied if the customer provides a valid foreign VAT/TIN and the substantive B2B tests are met; the supplier must retain service contracts, customer tax status evidence, and use-case documentation to support the territorial analysis. Services supplied to non-taxable overseas customers may qualify as outside scope or zero-rated only where specific CGI provisions apply and the supplier can substantiate offshore consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DELTA electronic export log / DAU-ENS) accepted by Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI)
Transport document proving physical exit from France and the EU: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR consignment note, or equivalent
Commercial invoice, packing list, purchase order, and bank financing evidence such as an Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 payment record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFIP and French Customs can retrospectively deny export or outside-scope treatment where supporting documentation is missing, forged, or otherwise insufficient. Reassessment triggers VAT clawback plus delayed-payment interest and the application of penalties under French tax law: 40% bad-faith penalty, 80% penalty for organised or fraudulent conduct, and criminal sanctions under Article 1741 CGI up to EUR 75,000 fine and five years' imprisonment. A false customs declaration can also lead to suspension or revocation of AEO/customs standing and exclusion from simplified OSS/IOSS schemes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), operating within the European System of Central Banks; foreign-exchange statistics and balance-of-payments compliance are co-administered with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) and the Direction Générale du Trésor of the French Ministry of Economy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully and freely convertible under EU law (Articles 63-66 TFEU); France maintains no exchange-control licensing regime for current-account items (SaaS licensing fees, hosting fees, service remuneration) or capital-account items (equity injections, shareholder loans, distributions). No profit-remittance authorization, conversion licence, or transfer restriction applies to OECD/EU counterparties. The de facto hurdles are limited to (i) the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical declaration ('motif'-coded cross-border payment reporting performed by the resident bank for transactions above EUR 12,500), (ii) French dividend withholding tax applicable to foreign shareholders (12.8% flat tax for individuals; 25% corporate withholding under Article 119 bis CGI, both reduced by applicable double-tax treaties), and (iii) the arm's-length and substance requirements applicable to intercompany treasury balances. None of these hurdles limits convertibility of the euro.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France enforces no export-proceeds surrender or forced conversion requirement: the mandatory conversion ratio is 0% and no statutory surrender timeline exists. Export receipts (SaaS subscription and cybersecurity service revenue) may be retained, pooled, and settled in any freely convertible currency. However, under EU monetary statistics Regulation (EC) No 184/2005 and the Banque de France balance-of-payments instruction, the resident exporter must ensure its intermediary bank reports cross-border receipts exceeding EUR 12,500 within five business days of month-end using the 'motif' (purpose-of-payment) taxonomy. Supporting documentary evidence (electronic invoices, licensing agreements) must be retained for at least five years.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Bloqué auprès du Dépositaire) / Operational Multi-Currency Account
Operational Account with Cash Management, FX Hedging and SWIFT Clearing
Capital Escrow Account / Commercial Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Mutuel / CIC (Crédit Industriel et Commercial)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for subscription-collection operations: regulated EU EMIs with an ACPR passport (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Memo Bank) and EU-passported digital banks (Revolut, N26) provide competitive IBAN-based SEPA C2B/B2B rails. Low for treasury-critical functions: EMIs are not full credit institutions and cannot (i) hold capital-escrow balances for SAS statutory capital-blocking certificates, (ii) file the Banque de France 'motif' balance-of-payments statistical declarations on behalf of the client, or (iii) execute USD/EUR/GBP FX hedging products. Non-EU/offshore EMIs (UK, US, HK licence) have no legal viability in France without an ACPR/ECB passport under PSD2; unlicensed firms engaging in French payment services commit the criminal offence of unlawful exercise of payment services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is legally permitted: French AML obligations (Monetary and Financial Code Art. R561-5, Decree No. 2019-1309) authorise video-KYC and electronic signature (eIDAS qualified certificates) for the SAS President and beneficial owners; physical presence is not a statutory mandate. In practice, Tier-1 French banks require a live video interview with the legal representative, a notarised/apostilled identity file for non-EU UBOs, and may require one physical signature appointment at the branch as a de facto internal policy, typically waivable for EU/EEA passport holders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) or parent company domiciled in a high-risk or sanctions-affiliated jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Extract Kbis of the SAS; (ii) UBO declaration (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filed with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; (iii) apostilled notarial identity documents and passport copies; (iv) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds attestation authenticated by an independent lawyer; (v) corporate organisational chart evidencing the whole ownership chain; (vi) evidence of real economic substance in France (registered office domiciliation agreement, payroll, leased premises).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector flag: cybersecurity / offensive-security SaaS perceived as dual-use or high technology-transfer risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) French SIREN/SIRET registration certificate; (ii) ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II attestations; (iii) penetration-testing engagement letters and vulnerability-disclosure programme documentation; (iv) statement from French export-control counsel confirming no classification under EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821; (v) blue-chip enterprise client list evidencing lawful commercial usage; (vi) documented end-user policies and purpose limitation controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Upstream capital injection from a foreign corporate shareholder (equity or shareholder loan) triggering PEP/sanctions and source-of-funds scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Shareholders' resolution and pacte d'associés; (ii) notarial or depositary certificate of fund blocking (attestation de dépôt des fonds) issued for the capital increase; (iii) loan agreement with repayment schedule for shareholder current-account advances; (iv) audited or management accounts of the foreign parent; (v) reference letter from the remitting foreign bank; (vi) pro-forma FX/MT103 authorisation naming the exact Banque de France 'motif' for direct investment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High projected cross-border turnover versus low French payroll and substance, triggering artificial-residence red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Employment contracts and French payroll evidence for the engineering and sales teams; (ii) French operational lease or professional domiciliation contract; (iii) engagement of a French expert-comptable (statutory accountant) with periodic financial filings; (iv) SaaS metrics (MRR/ARR, NRR, customer contracts) substantiating economic substance; (v) corporate VAT and CIT filing history or forward business plan, as applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder-loan flows are cleared by SWIFT MT103 over Target2 (EUR) or correspondent nostro rails (USD/GBP) into the SAS's French beneficiary account (IBAN FR76...; BIC of the receiving Tier-1 bank). The remitting bank must encode the Banque de France balance-of-payments 'motif' for direct investment ('Investissements directs - apport en capital') in SWIFT field 77B/remittance information; the receiving bank verifies against the statutory declaration threshold (EUR 12,500) and files the aggregated declaration within five business days of month-end. The founder must pre-deliver to the bank (a) the capital-increase deed and depositary fund-blocking certificate, (b) the shareholder resolution, and (c) a source-of-funds pack from the remitting institution; proceeds are released to the operational account only after the capital increase is registered with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cloud infrastructure (AWS/Azure/GCP), subcontractors, and software licences, the clearing rails are (i) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border non-EU settlements, with MT202 COV as cover when a correspondent intermediary is used; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Direct Debit Core/B2B for EU supplier payables and payroll, settled on Target2/TIPS; (iii) commercial card rails (Visa/Mastercard virtual corporate cards) for recurring platform purchases; and (iv) standby letters of credit (SBLC) or UCP 600 documentary credits only when counterparties in physical-infrastructure jurisdictions require bank payment undertakings, which is commercially atypical for SaaS treasury. Payment instructions must always carry the SAS's LEI/IBAN, the Banque de France export/import 'motif', and the underlying contract reference for audit traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Change à terme (deliverable FX forward, EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) — suitable when designated as a hedge of committed forecast exposure
Option de change (European-style FX options on EUR crosses) — purchased strategies only, avoiding net premium selling for unlicensed corporates
Swap de change (FX swap) for rolling EUR/USD treasury conversion without disturbing operational liquidity
Cross-currency swap (couverture de change croisée) for aligning long-term USD/EUR balance-sheet positions

NDF (non-deliverable forward) — permitted exclusively for regulated non-convertible emerging-market currencies (e.g., KRW, INR, TWD, BRL) where physical delivery is legally impossible; never for EUR-convertible pairs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels) — balance sheet, income statement, annexes, management report and allocation of net income as approved by shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (commercial court registry) and the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by INPI; e-formality lodged via Infogreffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: C. com. art. L232-21/L232-22: filing within one month of shareholder approval and in all cases within seven months of the fiscal-year close; for a 31-December year-end the outer limit is 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry issues a formal notice; if no deposit within one month, the public prosecutor may petition the court to compel filing under an astreinte (daily penalty); persistent failure constitutes grounds for judicial strike-off (radiation) from the RCS and exposes the president to civil liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats n°2065-SD with tax schedules) and settlement of the balance of corporate income tax (IS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP — Service des Impôts des Entreprises of the registered office; mandatory e-filing on impots.gouv.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year filer: 2065-SD return due no later than 3 May of the following year (next business day if 3 May falls on a weekend); non-calendar year: within three months of the fiscal close; balance of IS due by 15 April for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 5% surcharge of the assessed tax, increased to 10% when filed more than 30 days after formal notice (CGI art. 1728), plus late-payment interest of 0.40% per month (CGI art. 1727); the strike-off procedure may additionally be accelerated where no return and no accounts have been filed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual collective decision of SAS shareholders approving the annual accounts and allocating the net result (written consultation or ordinary general meeting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal record entered in the mandatory corporate minute-book (registre des décisions des associés); no deposit obligation except where the decision modifies capital, dissolves the company or is otherwise registrable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: C. com. art. L227-9: decision must be taken within six months of the fiscal-year close; the one-month accounts-deposit window begins on the date of that decision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No fixed administrative fine, but late approval invalidates the deposit window and blocks lawful dividend distribution; a company that repeatedly fails to hold the decision and file accounts is exposed to judicial strike-off and liability of the president for defective governance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) — annual verification and update within 30 days of any shareholding transfer that changes control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by INPI and filed with the commercial registry of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No anniversary-based annual UBO filing in France; update mandatory within 30 days after any change in the shareholding or control structure (C. mon. fin. art. L561-46 et seq.); the RNE re-compares the declaration with the share register at each annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or inaccurate declaration: fine up to €15,000 for the company and up to €15,000 / six months' imprisonment for the legal representative; consecutive non-compliance suspends registry filings and feeds the administrative strike-off process

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) is mandatory where the SAS exceeds at least two of the three following thresholds at the fiscal close: total balance-sheet assets over €4,000,000; net turnover (excl. VAT) over €8,000,000; average workforce over 50 (C. com. art. L227-9-1 and related decree). The audit is also compulsory if the SAS controls or is the consolidation head of a subgroup meeting the consolidated thresholds, or if shareholders holding at least one-third of the capital validly request one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French statutory accounts under the Plan Comptable Général (ANC Regulation 2016-10, codified at C. com. art. L123-12 et seq.); IFRS (EU-endorsed) applies only to consolidated accounts of listed EU companies and may be voluntarily used for consolidation purposes only — the individual annual accounts of an unlisted cybersecurity SaaS must remain prepared under French GAAP in EUR.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a separate calendar-year UBO certificate; the compliance protocol requires the SAS to (i) verify the declared beneficial owners at each annual accounts decision, (ii) record each share transfer in the share-transfer ledger, and (iii) file a new beneficial-owner declaration with the RNE/registry within 30 days of any transfer that changes ownership of more than 25% of capital or voting rights or that modifies ultimate control. The registry automatically reconciles the UBO record against the annual accounts deposit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des Mouvements de Titres (register of share transfers and Register of Members)
Registre des Décisions des Associés et du Président (SAS minute book and president's decisions)
Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (beneficial-owner register with the last RNE declaration receipt)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 – USD 800 (EUR 170 – EUR 700) per annum for a licensed commercial domiciliation agent in Paris; EUR 130 – EUR 400 in secondary cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,500 – USD 16,500 (EUR 6,000 – EUR 15,000) per annual statutory or voluntarily requested audit of a SaaS company below the CAC thresholds
